blueprint_topic: Management of Care — referral to evidence-based epilepsy self-management and psychosocial support resources
stem: A client living with epilepsy reports stress, stigma, missed appointments, and difficulty managing treatment day to day. Which referral best addresses these needs as an adjunct to ongoing medical care?

options.A: Refer to an epilepsy self-management program that builds skills for treatment follow-through, provider communication, stress, stigma, and resource use.
options.B: Refer to a general peer-support group for shared experiences, while leaving medication routines, appointments, and provider communication to routine clinic visits.
options.C: Refer for counseling focused on stress and stigma, and postpone epilepsy self-management training until seizures become harder to control.
options.D: Refer to a general wellness course on sleep and exercise without epilepsy-specific work on treatment routines, appointments, or health care communication.

rationale: A is correct. Current CDC guidance states that epilepsy self-management programs help people learn strategies and skills to make good health decisions and feel better while living with epilepsy. The CDC Managing Epilepsy Well Network specifically addresses common challenges such as staying on track with medications and appointments, communicating with health care providers, handling stress and mental-health challenges, dealing with stigma and memory problems, managing fatigue, and finding and using resources. CDC also lists tested programs that address stress, stigma, isolation, depression, cognition, communication, and day-to-day disease management. These programs complement prescribed treatment and professional follow-up rather than replacing them. B may provide useful social support but does not directly address the treatment-management and provider-communication deficits stated in the stem. C may appropriately address stress and stigma, but delaying self-management training until seizures worsen is unsupported; self-management resources are intended to help people manage epilepsy and its daily effects. D may reinforce healthy habits but omits the epilepsy-specific treatment, appointment, communication, and resource-management skills that match the client's stated problems.
educational_objective: Connect clients with epilepsy to evidence-based self-management resources that build treatment-management, communication, coping, and resource-use skills alongside ongoing medical care.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: Managing Epilepsy; Managing Epilepsy Well Network; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: CDC Managing Epilepsy and Managing Epilepsy Well Network dated 2024-05-15 and current when rechecked 2026-08-20; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: CDC 'Managing Epilepsy' dated May 15, 2024: self-management can improve quality of life; programs help people make good health decisions and feel better while living with epilepsy; CDC-funded programs include options addressing memory, provider-patient communication, depression, stress, stigma, isolation, and mental-health outcomes. CDC 'Managing Epilepsy Well Network' dated May 15, 2024: self-management programs develop strategies/skills and address medication and appointment adherence, provider communication, stress/mental-health challenges, stigma, memory, fatigue, and finding/using resources; the page states the network has created and tested multiple programs and identifies programs proven effective and available in some communities. NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Management of Care supports assessment of referral needs, multidisciplinary/community resources, education, and continuity of care.
source_claim_supported: Current CDC guidance directly supports evidence-based epilepsy self-management referral for the exact treatment-management, communication, stress, stigma, and resource-use concerns in the stem, as an adjunct to ongoing health care rather than a replacement for prescribed treatment.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: assess need for referrals, collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, provide education, update the plan of care, and utilize resources to promote quality client care.
pdf_visual_verification: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan printed page 7 / PDF pageno 10 was freshly screenshot-verified earlier in this continuation on 2026-08-20. CDC evidence used for Q1972 is current HTML; no CDC PDF evidence is used.
correction_summary: Original Q1972 included an absolute-word distractor and alternatives that were easy to eliminate because they denied recognized epilepsy concerns or substituted support for treatment. The item was rebuilt so each distractor represents a potentially useful but incomplete resource. Post-fetch review then tightened the correct option to remove a residual length/comprehensiveness cue while preserving the CDC-supported treatment-management, communication, stress/stigma, and resource-use domains.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly matches CDC MEW targets across treatment management, appointments, provider communication, stress/stigma, and resource use.
option_audit.B: Plausible social-support referral; incomplete because it leaves the client's treatment-management and provider-communication problems unaddressed.
option_audit.C: Plausible mental-health referral; counseling can help stress/stigma, but intentionally postponing epilepsy self-management training is unsupported and fails to address current management difficulties.
option_audit.D: Plausible general wellness referral; sleep/exercise can support health, but a generic program does not target the treatment, appointment, communication, and resource-management deficits in the stem.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on only/all/always/never/must-type absolute wording.
cueing_audit.answer_length: Final option lengths: A 151, B 163, C 138, D 154 characters; the correct answer is not the longest and the choices are substantially balanced.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are legitimate referral categories and differ by comprehensiveness and match to the stated needs rather than obvious correctness cues.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after the option refinement. B/C/D may each address one component of care but do not address the combined self-management deficits in the stem; A remains uniquely comprehensive and evidence-matched. Independent post-fetch reread remains required.
